CSAFP’s CORNER | WHEN RESTRAINT BECOMES COURAGE: BONIFACIO, DEMOCRACY, AND A SOLDIER’S OATH

In his latest Inquirer column, AFP Chief of Staff General Romeo S Brawner Jr. reflects on the legacy of Gat Andres Bonifacio, who fought for dignity, justice, and self-determination. General Brawner underscored, “From the leader of the Katipunan, we inherited a timeless truth: patriotism is not measured by power, but by principle—by the courage to do what is right, whatever the cost.”

This year’s Bonifacio Day became a reminder of democracy in action as Filipinos took to the streets seeking transparency and accountability. Amid these demonstrations, the AFP honored Bonifacio’s spirit with restraint and principle—protecting the people’s right to be heard while upholding the rule of law. This, General Brawner notes, is the strength of a professional military.

He stresses that the peaceful protests reaffirm a core democratic truth: democracy thrives when citizens speak and institutions listen. The AFP stood united, loyal to civilian authority, committed to constitutional order, and steadfast in its sworn duty to defend the Republic.

General Brawner reminds the nation that “The Constitution remains our common ground—where dissent is protected, power is limited, and the military remains firmly subordinate to civilian authority.” In every peaceful protest, in every institution fulfilling its mandate, and in every soldier choosing principle over ambition, the Republic proves its strength. This is how democracy endures. This is how courage is shown. This is how a soldier keeps faith with the nation.
